records.name: Frator Heru Institute
records.summary: Runs seminars, workshops and rites of passage programs, and has a curriculum project for state correctional facilities. Its website shows no dated events, so ask the office what is running.
records.what_you_do: Attend a seminar or workshop, or ask about the rites of passage program for young people.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us form on thefratorheruinstitute.org, or call (908) 334-1793, to ask about the next seminar or rites of passage program.
first_step.basis: Programs are named on the site, but no dates, prices or sign-up steps are shown, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The website does not describe what a seminar or rites of passage session is like, how long it runs, or who attends. The only listed ways to find out are the contact form and the phone line.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the next date, time and location before you go, because none are posted on the site.

records.notes: The site lists seminars, rites of passage, First World Komix, Human Race Studies, the State Correctional Curriculum Project, consulting and a store. The program pages name the topics but give no dates, prices or sign-up steps. Years that appear only in image file names were not counted as evidence. The contact page is a form only, with no email shown. Six fetches used, the per group cap.

records.name: Marian Anderson Neighborhood Academy Supporters
records.summary: A volunteer-led group that supports Marian Anderson Neighborhood Academy, a Philadelphia public school. It helps celebrate the school, raises money for its needs, and connects families with the school.
records.what_you_do: Help at school events, contribute items for in-school events, or join a committee such as fundraising, community engagement, or marketing and communication.

schedule.text: The board meets monthly, and each board member is expected to serve on at least one committee. Committees take new members at any point in the school year. Volunteers also help with recurring school events such as Movie Night and the Back to School Jam.

first_step.how: Fill in the Volunteer/Board Interest form linked from the Connect page, or help at a school event such as Movie Night or the Back to School Jam.
first_step.basis: The Connect page links a public interest form, and people can join a committee at any point in the school year. No dues or approval step is stated.
first_step.what_to_expect: Committees and events run through the school year. The board meets monthly, and each board member is expected to serve on at least one committee. The site does not give meeting times, a time commitment or dues, so ask when you fill in the form.
first_visit_tips: Ask about school district clearances before you sign up for classroom, field trip or after-school club help.
Subscribe to the MANAS newsletter, or follow the group on Facebook or Instagram, to hear about events.

records.notes: School-day volunteer roles (chaperoning, classroom help, after-school clubs) need school district clearances, per the Connect page. The clearance field is left out because the newcomer role is not known, and event volunteering is not stated to need them. The Fun Day post is dated May 29 and its title says 2026, so last_sign_of_life is 2026-05. The Night Out fundraiser is listed for March 21, 2026 on the FAQ; it is not recorded as a dated event.

records.name: Friends of Columbus Square
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Columbus Square park. They host park cleanups, outdoor movie nights, and neighborhood events, and they want the park to be a shared space for everyone nearby.
records.what_you_do: Pitch in at park cleanups, come to outdoor movie nights and neighborhood events, and join the mailing list to hear about the next one.

schedule.text: Park cleanups, outdoor movie nights, neighborhood events and public meetings. The site lists no dates; the group announces them through its mailing list and social media.

cost.text: The site does not state a cost for events.

first_step.how: Join the group's mailing list (the sign-up link on columbussquare.org) to hear about the next cleanup, movie night or public meeting.
first_step.basis: The calendar page says visitors are welcome at public meetings and volunteer events, and the mailing list is the clear way to hear about them. The site does not describe what a first cleanup involves.
first_step.what_to_expect: Cleanups, movie nights and public meetings are open to visitors, and the site invites new people to join. Dates are not posted on the site, so the mailing list or social media is where to check. The site does not say how long a cleanup runs or what to bring.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the mailing list first, since the website does not post dates.
Email friends@columbussquare.org before you come if you want to know what to bring.

records.notes: The events calendar is an embedded Google Calendar whose entries did not load in the reader, so no event dates are recorded. The About page names other volunteer leaders than the tier 1 contact, so the contact name may be out of date and is flagged for a later check. The contact page gives one email and no phone number.

records.name: Crease Street Garden
records.summary: Neighbors who look after the Crease Street Garden in Fishtown. They tend the beds, hold work days announced to a mailing list, and let groups book the space for gatherings.
records.what_you_do: Join a work day, when the garden holds one.

schedule.text: Garden work days are announced through the mailing list. The site shows no work day dates.

cost.text: Joining the mailing list is free. Reserving the garden is free for up to 25 guests in 3-hour slots, and donations are welcome.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list, or email friendsofcreasestgarden@gmail.com, to ask about the next work day.
first_step.basis: The mailing list and email are clear ways to ask, but the site gives no open days or sign-up steps for work days, so it is not clear a newcomer can join one.
first_step.what_to_expect: Work days are announced by email and the mailing list, and the site does not list dates or describe what a work day involves. The garden is a shared green space, and it closes at dusk.
first_visit_tips: Leave dogs at home, since the garden does not allow them.
Take your trash home with you.
Plan to leave before dusk, when the garden closes.

records.notes: The booking page's Upcoming Events panel did not load, so no work day dates were visible. The 2025-03 date comes from the upload folder of an obituary PDF linked on the home page. Garden rules on the home page: no dogs, respect neighbors and plants, take trash home, no open fires, and leave by dusk.

records.name: Friends of Three Bears Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Three Bears Park on Delancey Street: they raise money through community events, keep the park clean and planted, and host seasonal gatherings such as an Easter egg hunt.
records.what_you_do: Help with the spring Love Your Park clean-up or a fall festival, or come out to Park after Dark and the Halloween event.

schedule.text: Clean-ups and park events through the year: a spring Love Your Park clean-up, a fall festival, Park after Dark, a Halloween event, and an Easter egg hunt. The events page lists no exact dates.

cost.text: Events and volunteering have no listed fees. The group invites donations at giving levels from $150 to $500 on its membership page, and it pays for upkeep through its own fundraisers.

first_step.how: Email threebearspark@gmail.com to ask about the next clean-up or park event and how to help.
first_step.basis: Events and clean-ups are public and an email address is listed, but the site does not say how to volunteer or what a clean-up involves.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a clean-up or event in detail, or say how long one lasts. Events are community days and fundraisers held through the year. The park is open every day from dawn to dusk, and no dates are posted, so ask by email before you come.
first_visit_tips: Email ahead, since the site does not post dates for clean-ups.
The park is open from dawn to dusk, every day of the year.

records.notes: The events page shows 2026 only in image file names, which were not counted as dated evidence. The membership page lists donor levels of $150, $250 and $500 and does not say what each includes. The footer social icons point to the website builder's own accounts, so no social link is recorded.

records.name: Friends of Eastern State Penitentiary Park
records.summary: Volunteers who care for the green spaces around Eastern State Penitentiary: they pick up trash, plant trees, run community events, and keep garden plots and playground areas in shape.
records.what_you_do: Join a trash pickup or tree planting day, help at a community event, or take on a garden plot.

schedule.text: Group leaders host work days through the year. Neighbor Nights run on the last Thursday of the month from May to September, a casual family night outdoors with food, music and games. Treecycling, a holiday tree drop-off, runs on the first two weekends of January. The site shows no dates for the work days.

locations.label: Corinthian Gardens, Brown Street Lawn and Playpen Playground

cost.text: Volunteering and events have no listed fees. Garden plot holders renew a $50 membership each year, and financial help is available.

first_step.how: Email Corinthiangardens19130@gmail.com or fespp19130@gmail.com to ask about the next work day or volunteer opening.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page is public and gives email addresses to ask. It does not say whether work days need approval, orientation or dues.
first_step.what_to_expect: Group leaders run work days through the year, and the tasks listed include weeding shared beds and mulching paths. The volunteer page does not give dates, orientation, or what to wear. Volunteering has no listed fee.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come, because work day dates are not posted.
To get a garden plot, plan on 15 volunteer hours and one FESPP event the year before. Plots are assigned in March.

records.notes: Mailing address is PO Box 15001, Philadelphia, PA 19130; 2198 Brown Street does not accept mail. Neighbor Nights and Treecycling are listed without a year, so they are recorded as yearly events, not dated ones. Plot rules: plots are assigned by availability each March; plot holders need 15 volunteer hours and one FESPP event each year, and pay a $50 yearly membership. Corinthian Gardens has its own volunteer email, listed on the volunteer page.

records.name: Friends of Historic Sedgeley
records.summary: Supporters who help keep up the Sedgeley Club Boathouse and the Turtle Rock lighthouse on Boathouse Row. They invite volunteers and gifts, and they welcome visitors to the boathouse.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the volunteer page, give or sponsor, or come visit the boathouse on Kelly Drive.

schedule.text: The boathouse is open to visitors on set days, with informal tours that the group arranges with Sedgeley Club members. The site does not list upcoming open days, so check the blog or email for dates.

cost.text: The site invites gifts and sponsorships. No fees were listed.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the Volunteer page (name, address, phone and email are required), or email info@friendsofhistoricsedgeley.org to ask about visiting or volunteering.
first_step.basis: Public visits on set days let a newcomer see the boathouse first. The volunteer form is the only listed way in, and the site does not describe roles or an orientation, so the way in is not clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open days are set by the group and include informal tours with Sedgeley Club members. The site does not say how long a visit takes, whether volunteer shifts have set hours, or what roles exist. No visit fee is listed.
first_visit_tips: Check the blog or email for the next open day, since none are listed on the visit page.
Use the contact address to ask what a volunteer does before you fill in the form.

records.notes: The contact page gives 15 Kelly Drive as the mailing address; the location keeps the boathouse address from tier 1. The only dated item is a 2025 blog post about a free Lighthouse Day open house on Saturday, August 9, 2025, 10 AM to 2 PM. No 2026 visit dates are shown. Visiting hours, parking and transit are not stated.
